anomalies.observed: On the AVR-ISP-6 header J1 the SCK pin (pin 3) is drawn on net NET0005, the same net that runs to the fan connector J9 pin 3. The ATtiny's SCK pin PB2 (U1 pin 7 / U4 pin 7) is on a different net, NET0003, which instead goes to the I2C headers J5/J7. The other three ISP signals do match the MCU: MISO (J1.1) = NET0004 = PB1, MOSI (J1.4) = NET0011 = PB0, RST (J1.5) = NET0009 = PB5.
anomalies.expected: The ISP clock must reach the ATtiny's SCK pin, i.e. J1 pin 3 should be on the same net as PB2 (NET0003), exactly as the MISO/MOSI/RESET pins of J1 are on the same nets as PB1/PB0/PB5.

evidence.quote: J1 AVR-ISP-6: MISO 1 -> NET0004, MOSI 4 -> NET0011, SCK 3 -> NET0005, RST 5 -> NET0009
U1 ATtiny13V-10S: PB0 5 -> NET0011, PB1 6 -> NET0004, PB2 7 -> NET0003, PB3 2 -> NET0002, PB4 3 -> NET0012, RESET/PB5 1 -> NET0009

anomalies.impact: The ATtiny never receives the ISP serial clock, so in-circuit programming through J1 will fail (no SCK to PB2); instead the ISP SCK pin is tied to the fan connector's pin 3, merging the programming clock with the fan interface.

parsed.summary: The ISP header's SCK pin (J1.3) is on net NET0005, which also runs to the fan connector J9, while the ATtiny's actual SCK pin PB2 is on net NET0003 — so the programming clock does not reach the microcontroller, unlike MISO/MOSI/RESET which do match the MCU. This looks like a routing/net-label error around the SCK line.
